questions.q: What problem does the ServiceNow DevOps app exist to solve?
options: That developers cannot write JavaScript in Studio
That ServiceNow instances cannot run any automated tests
That Update Sets cannot be previewed before committing
That an external CI/CD pipeline can deploy code with no connection to ServiceNow's governed Change Management process
questions.explain: Without something bridging the two, a pipeline's deployments are invisible to Change Enablement — not by design, just because nothing connects them.

questions.q: Is ServiceNow DevOps itself a CI/CD engine that builds and deploys code?
options: No — it only stores documentation about pipelines, with no real tracking
No — it tracks and orchestrates delivery activity around the platform, while the actual build/deploy work happens in external tools
Yes — it is ServiceNow's own build server
Yes — it fully replaces tools like Jenkins or GitHub Actions
questions.explain: The DevOps app sits alongside external pipeline tools and ServiceNow's ITSM/Change capabilities — it doesn't replace the pipeline engine itself.

questions.q: What is the core capability of ServiceNow DevOps most relevant to this course?
options: Automatically creating or updating Change Request records to match real CI/CD pipeline events
Generating ATF test scripts without any human review
Automatically writing all of an application's business rules
Replacing the need for Update Sets entirely, platform-wide
questions.explain: That automatic Change Request tracking is what keeps pipeline-driven deployments inside governed Change Management instead of bypassing it.

questions.q: When a pipeline event triggers an automatically created Change Request, is that Change Request treated differently from a manually created one?
options: No — it's a real, governed record subject to the same Change Enablement rules from Course 8
No — but it is not visible to anyone in Change Management
Yes — it cannot be linked back to the pipeline run that created it
Yes — it skips CAB review entirely by default, with no exceptions
questions.explain: Automation changes how the record gets created, not whether it's a legitimate, governed Change Request once it exists.

questions.q: Why does this lesson matter for understanding Lesson 18's integration pattern and Lesson 19's change-velocity tension?
options: Because Change Enablement from Course 8 is no longer relevant once DevOps is introduced
Because ServiceNow DevOps has no relationship to CI/CD pipelines at all
Because Lesson 18 and 19 replace everything taught in this lesson
Because both later lessons assume ServiceNow DevOps already exists to keep pipeline activity connected to governed Change records
questions.explain: Lesson 18 covers how the connection actually works, and Lesson 19 covers the tension that connection creates — both build directly on this foundation.
